decks.module: The manual and the Class D license

cards.front: What is a Class D license, and what does it cover without restrictions?
cards.back: A Class D license is the non commercial license, and without restrictions it covers any motor vehicle except a commercial motor vehicle.

cards.front: Which manuals do commercial drivers and motorcycle endorsement seekers use?
cards.back: Truck, bus and other commercial or public service drivers use the Commercial Driver License manual, while motorcycle endorsement seekers use the Motorcycle Operator manual.

cards.front: Which vehicles does this manual's Class D license cover, and who studies other manuals?
cards.back: This manual and its Class D license cover passenger vehicles only, while truck and bus drivers study the Commercial Driver License manual and riders study the Motorcycle Operator manual.

cards.front: Where should readers check for the latest laws, documents and test appointments?
cards.back: Readers should check ct.gov slash dmv for the latest laws, the required document list, and the online knowledge test appointment.

decks.module: Why new drivers are at risk

cards.front: What does the manual say about crashes and young drivers aged fifteen to nineteen?
cards.back: Crashes are the top killer of fifteen to nineteen year olds, strike mostly in the first two licensed years, and peak in the first six months.

cards.front: What does the manual say about the brain region that judges risk?
cards.back: The brain region that judges risk keeps maturing into the middle twenties, leaving teens short on hazard judgment.

cards.front: How do teen passengers affect crash risk, and what must families do?
cards.back: Teen passenger loads raise crash risk, so families must enforce the state passenger limits at home.

cards.front: Why must the state curfew be enforced for young drivers?
cards.back: Night hours bring deadlier crashes and drowsy driving danger for the young, so the state curfew must be enforced.

cards.front: What does the manual say about teens and seat belts?
cards.back: Teens wear belts least, yet buckling up is the simplest shield against crash death and grave injury.

cards.front: What rule do teens face on drinking, and why?
cards.back: Teens face zero tolerance: a single drink already harms driving skill and crash odds.

cards.front: Which in-car distractions does the manual say raise serious crash risk?
cards.back: Calls, passengers, texts, radio tuning, loose pets and like distractions inside the car all lift serious crash risk.

cards.front: What must a driver have before any practice driving?
cards.back: No practice driving starts without a learner permit, and the holder carries it on every drive.

cards.front: How old must a learner permit applicant be?
cards.back: Permit applicants must be at least sixteen years old.

cards.front: How does a qualified applicant receive the photo learner permit?
cards.back: DMV mails a new photo learner permit to each qualified applicant.

cards.front: What health standards must permit applicants meet?
cards.back: Applicants must meet license holder health and fitness standards, and risky medical conditions need a favorable review before any permit issues.

cards.front: Whom should applicants facing a possible medical review call, and when?
cards.back: Applicants facing a possible medical review should call the Driver Services Division well ahead at (eight hundred sixty) two hundred sixty-three-five thousand seven hundred twenty.

cards.front: How long does a learner permit last?
cards.back: A permit lasts until the driver licenses or for two years from issue, whichever ends first.

cards.front: What ends a learner permit?
cards.back: A permit ends at licensing or at two years from issue, so an early license beats the calendar and a slow learner faces expiry.

cards.front: What can happen if a driver ignores the permit rules?
cards.back: Ignoring permit rules can suspend the permit.

cards.front: Which two tests does the learner permit require?
cards.back: The permit demands passing a vision test plus a twenty five question knowledge test.

cards.front: How is the knowledge test scheduled, and when can the road test be booked?
cards.back: Knowledge tests run by appointment with online booking and payment, and the road test books only after the knowledge pass.

cards.front: According to the driver's manual, how long is the knowledge test and what does passing take?
cards.back: The knowledge test spans twenty five questions with twenty correct needed to pass, follows this manual, and offers samples on the DMV mobile app.

cards.front: According to the driver's manual, which two numbers describe the knowledge test?
cards.back: The knowledge test counts twenty five questions but only twenty correct answers, so the length and the pass mark are two different numbers to keep apart.

cards.front: How are the vision screening and the knowledge test related?
cards.back: Vision screening and the knowledge test are separate permit gates: one checks eyesight minimums and the other checks manual knowledge, and both must be passed.

cards.front: What vision standard applies to every license class, and what applies to an applicant blind in one eye?
cards.back: Every license class requires vision of at least twenty over forty with or without glasses or contacts; an applicant blind in one eye needs twenty over forty and a visual field of at least one hundred degrees in the other eye.

cards.front: How does the vision rule differ for one-eyed applicants?
cards.back: Standard applicants meet twenty over forty vision in general, but one eyed applicants must show twenty over forty plus a one hundred degree field in the remaining eye.

cards.front: What can happen if you drive without required corrective lenses?
cards.back: Driving without required corrective lenses risks a citation at a law enforcement stop.

cards.front: How often does the manual suggest a specialist eye check?
cards.back: Eyes deserve a specialist check every year or two, since weak vision hides without testing.
cards.memory_hook: eye check every year or two

cards.front: Where does the instructor sit, and what are the instructor's duties?
cards.back: The instructor rides in the front passenger seat, stays alert and ready to take control, and shares responsibility for safe operation with the driver.

cards.front: Whom may sixteen- and seventeen-year-old permit holders carry as passengers?
cards.back: Permit holders of sixteen and seventeen take no passengers except a licensed instructor giving lessons plus companions, or one instructing person at least twenty years old, licensed four or more straight years with no suspension in the prior four.

cards.front: When does the permit passenger ban lift?
cards.back: The passenger ban lifts during live lessons from a licensed instructor of a commercial school or driver education program.

cards.front: Who may teach a teen at home?
cards.back: Home teaching falls to a qualifier of twenty plus with four suspension free licensed years: a parent, foster parent, guardian, grandparent, married minor’s spouse, or failing those an uncle, aunt, sibling, or stepparent.

cards.front: When does the instructing adult count as the one allowed passenger?
cards.back: A twenty plus adult with four suspension free licensed years may instruct a teen permit holder, but that same adult counts as the single allowed passenger only while actively instructing.

cards.front: Which class must every first-time license seeker finish, and where?
cards.back: First time license seekers of every age must finish an eight hour Safe Driving Practices class at a Connecticut commercial driving school before licensing.

cards.front: What are the three ways teen applicants can train?
cards.back: Teen applicants train via a licensed commercial school, a high school program, or home training topped with an eight hour safe driving course holding two parent training hours.

cards.front: What must each teen permit holder's parent or guardian complete?
cards.back: Each teen permit holder’s parent or guardian completes two teaching hours on under eighteen law and teen driving perils inside the required eight hour program.

cards.front: Who must complete the eight-hour Safe Driving Practices course before obtaining a Connecticut license?
cards.back: Connecticut law requires anyone of any age who has not previously held a Connecticut license and does not hold a valid out-of-state license to complete an eight-hour Safe Driving Practices course at a Connecticut commercial driving school before obtaining a license.

cards.front: What does a school course combine, and which form does it end with?
cards.back: School courses join thirty classroom hours to forty or more coached road hours, ending in form CS-one, the ticket to the road test.

cards.front: Which form do home-trained drivers file, and what must the course include?
cards.back: Home trained drivers also file form CS-1a for an approved eight hour course spending four plus hours on alcohol and drug effects, use dangers, abuse penalties, and the mandatory two hour parent class.

cards.front: How do forms CS-one and CS-one-a differ?
cards.back: Form CS-one certifies school course completion for road test eligibility, whereas form CS-1a certifies the home trainer’s eight hour alcohol syllabus course, and the two forms are not interchangeable.

cards.front: What does the home teacher sign off at the road test?
cards.back: At the road test the home teacher signs off the permit, thirty study hours with the eight hour Safe Driving Practices class, full manual coverage, forty coached road hours, and the two hour parent class.

cards.front: What must out-of-state licensed teens of sixteen and seventeen do for a Connecticut license?
cards.back: Out of state licensed teens of sixteen and seventeen must also take the eight hour course for a Connecticut license.

decks.module: Waiting periods before the road test

cards.front: How long do school graduates wait for the road test, compared with other applicants?
cards.back: School graduates test after one hundred twenty permit days; all other applicants wait one hundred eighty days to the driving exam.

cards.front: Which training mix unlocks testing after the shorter wait?
cards.back: Thirty classroom hours plus eight commercial coached road hours unlock testing at one hundred twenty days; everyone else waits one hundred eighty days past the permit.

cards.front: Which wait belongs only to the school path?
cards.back: School trained applicants wait one hundred twenty days for the road test while all others wait one hundred eighty days, and the shorter wait belongs only to the school path.

cards.front: How do the school and home hour mixes compare with the thirty-plus-eight shortcut?
cards.back: Thirty classroom hours pair with forty coached road hours for school teens, while home teens log thirty study hours plus forty road hours, and neither mix matches the thirty plus eight shortcut to the shorter wait.

recaps.module: Why new drivers are at risk

recap_hooks.text: Crashes are the top killer of teens aged fifteen to nineteen, with the danger greatest in the first six months of licensed driving.
Teen passengers, night driving, skipped belts, any drinking and in-car distractions all raise the risk.
Applicants must be at least sixteen, and no practice driving starts without a learner permit.
The permit lasts until licensing or two years from issue, whichever ends first.
The permit needs a vision test and a knowledge test, and the road test is booked only after the knowledge pass.
According to the driver's manual, the knowledge test has twenty five questions and twenty correct answers pass it.
Teen permit holders take no passengers except a lesson from a licensed instructor or one qualified instructing adult.
Every first-time applicant takes the eight-hour Safe Driving Practices class, and teen families add the two-hour parent block.
School courses end with form CS-one, while home-trained drivers file form CS-one-a.
